definitions.explanation: A humble expression for borrowing something from a respected person. Used when referring to borrowing with respect toward the lender.

examples.japanese: お{知恵|ちえ}を{拝借|はいしゃく}できますか。
examples.english: May I ask for your wisdom?
examples.notes: Common set phrase for asking advice

examples.japanese: {少々|しょうしょう}お{時間|じかん}を{拝借|はいしゃく}できますでしょうか。
examples.english: Could I have a moment of your time?

examples.japanese: こちらのペンを{拝借|はいしゃく}してもよろしいでしょうか。
{先生|せんせい}のお{力|ちから}を{拝借|はいしゃく}したいのですが。
examples.english: I would like to ask for your help.

notes:
KEIGO ({敬語|けいご}): {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language). The prefix {拝|はい} indicates humble respect toward the person from whom something is borrowed.

VERB FORM:
・{拝借|はいしゃく}する (to borrow - humble)
・{拝借|はいしゃく}いたす (more formal humble form)

COMMON SET PHRASES:
・お{知恵|ちえ}を{拝借|はいしゃく}する (to ask for someone's wisdom/advice)
・お{時間|じかん}を{拝借|はいしゃく}する (to take someone's time)
・お{力|ちから}を{拝借|はいしゃく}する (to ask for someone's help)

CONTEXTS: Used in formal business settings, meetings, and when making requests of superiors or respected individuals.

RELATED {拝|はい} COMPOUNDS:
・{拝見|はいけん} - to see/look at (humble)
・{拝読|はいどく} - to read (humble)
・{拝聴|はいちょう} - to listen (humble)
・{拝受|はいじゅ} - to receive (humble)

PLAIN EQUIVALENT: {借|か}りる (to borrow - neutral)
